questions.question: In planning a TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV procedure, which CT-derived measurements most directly predict coronary obstruction risk (e.g., coronary ostial height, sinus of Valsalva width, valve-to-coronary [VTC] distance, and anticipated neo-skirt height), and how would each parameter influence the decision to proceed without protection versus perform BASILICA or planned coronary wiring and chimney stenting?

Immediately after the third TAVI, the mean gradient was 67 mm Hg with an AVA of 0.9 cm² and DVI 0.24. What are the leading causes of an early high transvalvular gradient after valve-in-valve TAVI, and what tests or imaging (e.g., Doppler indices, acceleration time, leaflet-motion CT, anticoagulation trial for suspected leaflet thrombosis) help distinguish prosthesis–patient mismatch from valve underexpansion, malposition, or thrombosis?

After treated prosthetic valve endocarditis due to Enterococcus faecalis, what clinical, microbiologic, and imaging criteria should be met before considering repeat TAVI (e.g., symptom status, negative serial blood cultures, absence of vegetations or paravalvular complications on TEE/CT), and how do contemporary guidelines frame the role of TAVI versus surgery in this setting?

What pathophysiologic mechanisms likely contributed to prosthetic valve failure in this patient (post-infectious leaflet injury/fibrosis, progressive structural degeneration, mechanical leaflet restriction), and how can high implantation in a redo TAVI help pin prior leaflets, limit neo-skirt formation, and improve the effective orifice area and coronary flow?

Why might a supra-annular, self-expanding valve with relatively low frame height and favorable commissural-alignment capability (e.g., Acurate neo2) be advantageous in a triple-stented anatomy, and how do these design features affect residual effective orifice area, gradients, and the likelihood of maintaining future coronary access?

Which implantation strategies during TAV-in-TAV(-in-TAV) optimize future coronary reaccess (e.g., commissural alignment, high implantation to keep neo-skirt below ostia, orientation to known coronary takeoff, avoidance of commissural posts in front of ostia), and what are the trade-offs with hemodynamics and anchoring?

How do you calculate and interpret the Doppler Velocity Index (DVI) and indexed aortic valve area (AVAi) after prosthetic valve implantation, and what thresholds support severe stenosis and/or severe prosthesis–patient mismatch in a post-TAVI valve-in-valve scenario?

Given the patient’s EuroSCORE II of 27% and prior endocarditis now resolved, what elements of multidisciplinary heart-team reasoning favor a third transcatheter intervention over surgery (e.g., prohibitive surgical anatomy with integrated prior frames, comorbidities like COPD/diabetes/GI bleeding, CT-demonstrated feasibility), and how should lifetime management be incorporated at the time of the first TAVI?

In a patient with prior transfemoral access complications (pseudoaneurysm requiring surgery), what preprocedural and intraprocedural steps reduce vascular risk during redo TAVI (e.g., CT iliofemoral sizing and calcium/burden assessment, ultrasound-guided puncture, pre-closure strategies, alternative access planning such as transaxillary/carotid, and bailout readiness)?
